key_insight: Replacing B-spline bases in Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks with adaptive radial basis functions (Free-RBFs) yields a KAN variant that keeps or improves approximation accuracy while drastically reducing computational overhead and implementation complexity.
problem_solved: Traditional KANs rely on B-spline basis functions and De Boor's algorithm, which are computationally expensive and cumbersome to implement; prior RBF-based KANs traded efficiency for accuracy. This paper resolves the trade-off by introducing adaptive RBFs that are both efficient to evaluate and flexible enough to preserve or improve accuracy.
method: Introduce Free-RBF-KAN: replace B-spline bases with trainable radial basis functions whose centers, scales, and amplitudes are learned end-to-end.
Design lightweight, differentiable RBF layers and initialization/regularization strategies that stabilize training and retain KAN’s universal approximation properties.
Demonstrate empirically that Free-RBF-KAN reduces evaluation cost (no De Boor recursion), speeds up training/inference, and matches or surpasses accuracy of prior KAN and RBF-KAN variants.
impact: Free-RBF-KAN makes Kolmogorov–Arnold-style universal approximators practical for resource-constrained and real-time settings, enabling faster function learning with simpler code and lower runtime cost for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: KAN decomposition with B-spline block crossed out and Free-RBF blocks replacing it, showing trainable centers/scales
Bar chart: runtime (inference/training) and memory comparison of B-spline KAN vs standard RBF-KAN vs Free-RBF-KAN
Accuracy vs. complexity plot: approximation error against number of basis functions, highlighting Pareto improvement
Heatmap or example function reconstructions: target function vs B-spline KAN vs Free-RBF-KAN for qualitative comparison
paper_title: Free-RBF-KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with Adaptive Radial Basis Functions for Efficient Function Learning
paper_authors: Shao-Ting Chiu, Siu Wun Cheung, Ulisses Braga-Neto, Chak Shing Lee, Rui Peng Li
